title: India's Got Latent Is Back. Alia Bhatt Is the First Guest. And the Internet Is Furious.
excerpt: Samay Raina's cult YouTube show returns for Season 2 with Bollywood's biggest star on the panel. Fans say the vibe is already dead.
body:
A leaked photograph from The Habitat in Mumbai on May 18 confirmed what the internet had been whispering for weeks: India's Got Latent is coming back, and its first guest is Alia Bhatt.

The image, clicked by an audience member during what appears to be a taping session, shows Bhatt in a grey t-shirt and black cap holding a microphone, sitting alongside her *Alpha* co-star Sharvari, with comedians Balraj Ghai and Aashish Solanki rounding out the panel. Within hours, the photo was everywhere. Reddit exploded. X was on fire. And the consensus from fans was not what you would expect.

They are not happy.

## The Show That Broke Indian YouTube

For anyone who has not followed India's Got Latent, here is the short version: comedian Samay Raina created a talent show on YouTube that was equal parts chaos, dark humor, and genuine unpredictability. Contestants performed, got roasted, and sometimes roasted right back. It became a cultural phenomenon among young Indians, particularly in the diaspora, where NRIs shared clips obsessively and argued about episodes in group chats across time zones.

Then it all went sideways. In February 2025, an episode featuring podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia spiraled into a nationwide controversy over an explicit joke about parents. Multiple FIRs were filed. Episodes were made private. The show effectively went dark.

Samay Raina spent months in a strange public limbo, eventually releasing a stand-up special called *Still Alive* that was part comedy, part therapy, part mea culpa. He confirmed Season 2 was in the works. He announced a global tour starting June 5 in Cologne and ending July 20 in Sydney, spanning cities with massive NRI populations.

And now, the comeback episode features Alia Bhatt promoting her upcoming YRF spy thriller *Alpha* (releasing July 10).

## Why Fans Are Disappointed

The backlash is not about Alia Bhatt personally. It is about what her presence signals.

India's Got Latent became a phenomenon precisely because it was not a Bollywood promotion vehicle. The magic of the show was its rawness, the feeling that anything could happen, that the comedian host was in charge and the guests were genuinely uncomfortable. When unknown contestants showed up and got demolished, or when someone turned the tables on the panel, that was the content that made the show special.

Bollywood stars promoting films on comedy shows is the oldest trick in the Indian entertainment playbook. Every talk show, every reality show, every weekend variety hour eventually becomes a conveyor belt for film promotions. Fans on Reddit and X are openly saying that India's Got Latent was supposed to be different.

"The essence of the show will go away," wrote one user. "It will only stay relevant for film promotions now."

Others are more pragmatic. The show has become "very big now," and big shows attract big guests, and big guests come with promotional agendas. That is the economics of Indian entertainment, and Samay Raina may not have the leverage to resist it.

## The Diaspora Angle

For NRIs, India's Got Latent occupied a unique cultural space: it was genuinely funny content from India that did not need subtitles, did not require context about which serial was trending, and felt like it belonged to the internet generation rather than the television generation. It traveled globally in a way that most Indian entertainment simply does not.

Season 2 is reportedly moving from YouTube to a premium OTT platform, possibly Netflix or Prime Video. If true, that makes it directly accessible to the diaspora audience without geographic restrictions, but it also raises the question of whether the show's unfiltered energy can survive the content moderation standards of a global streaming platform.

Samay Raina's upcoming global tour suggests he understands where his most engaged audience lives: Germany, the UK, Australia, the US, all cities with dense NRI communities. The show's future may depend more on the diaspora than on Indian domestic audiences.

Whether Season 2 can recapture the lightning-in-a-bottle energy of the original while navigating Bollywood promotional obligations and OTT content standards remains the biggest question in Indian digital entertainment right now.

*Alpha, starring Alia Bhatt and Sharvari, releases July 10, 2026. India's Got Latent Season 2 premiere date is yet to be announced.*
